Therefore f(−2/p)<0, f(0)=1 and f(t)→+∞ as t→−∞, yielding ≥2 negative real roots; positive quartic discriminant then forces four simple real roots, and positive coefficients eliminate nonnegative roots. Independently regenerated mixed hollow/interior cubic discriminant 75 strictly positive monomials (constant900), hollow/hollow cubic discriminant25 positive terms, and the two degenerate quadratic discriminants 3(3U²+6UV+10U+3V²+2V+3)>0 and 3(3U²+4U+4)>0. These cover all b=0 or d=0 boundary cases including degree drops. This is exhaustive symbolic coefficient positivity over nonnegative integer parameters, not extrapolated polygon sampling; the embedded 118477-byte coefficient JSON file was not separately matched byte-for-byte in this independent script, but its claimed polynomial positivity was recomputed directly.

originality.rationale: Originality PASS, qualified. The established Wagner/Brändén–Ferroni–Jochemko Hadamard preservation theorem assumes every input h*-polynomial is already real-rooted. Every 2D polygon factor fails real-rootedness only when B=3 and I=1,2,3. The examined 2026 Liu survey applies the same hypothesis and does not imply those exceptional primitive-edge triangle cases. The complete all-polygon theorem is thus a sharper universal result with a verified genuinely non-real-rooted input example. The real novelty is exactly the exceptional family and simple roots, not the preexisting product-of-real-rooted factors principle.
residual_risks: An older unindexed special case for primitive-edge triangles multiplied by arbitrary polygons could cover the new remainder; priority search is bounded.
Only relevant statements/sections rather than all appendices of the 59-page Liu survey were inspected in depth; no universal whole-document noncoverage claim is made.

value.rationale: Scientific value PASS: real-rootedness of h* polynomials is a central strong combinatorial regularity property, and Cartesian product is natural in Ehrhart/Segre geometry. The theorem closes a genuine exception left out by otherwise powerful input-real-rootedness preservation, proving all products of 2D lattice polygons have simple strictly negative roots despite explicit non-real-rooted factors. The universal integer-parameter discriminant certificate and exact exceptional triangle example give a useful nontrivial preservation phenomenon.
residual_risks: The proof is a controlled finite symbolic-algebra certificate rather than a conceptual classification across higher-dimensional factors; the theorem does not extend outside the specified dimension-two inputs.

final_claim: For any full-dimensional lattice polygons P,Q⊂R², h*_(P×Q)(t) has only distinct strictly negative real zeros of its actual degree. Its coefficients are explicit in (I_P,B_P,I_Q,B_Q), including non-real-rooted primitive-edge triangle factors (B=3, I=1,2,3); e.g. (1+t+t²)×(1+t+t²) yields 1+11t+30t²+11t³+t⁴=(t²+4t+1)(t²+7t+1).
